decisionTitle: task_11.json has empty filesToEdit and a root-level unitTestCmd ("npm test") that is not case-converter-scoped; --out implemented as duplicate-to-stdout-and-file per architecture.md, not suppress-stdout
rationale:
task_11.json listed no filesToEdit and unitTestCmd literally as "npm test" (no --prefix, unlike task_10.json's "npm --prefix case-converter test"). The repository root is itself an unrelated decoy npm package ("tekstovyy-kvest", a toy text-quest state machine under lib/state-machine.js + test/skeleton.test.js, per package.json description "Игрушечный консольный проект для гейта M16а"), whose own scripts.test is `node --test`. Because Node's default test-runner discovery recurses from cwd and picks up every *.test.js under the whole /workspace tree, running `npm test` from the repo root happens to also execute case-converter's new tests (and every other utility's tests) as a side effect, not because the two projects are actually related — I verified this by running both `npm test` at the root (294/294 passed, spanning all ten utilities plus the decoy project) and the properly scoped `npm --prefix case-converter test` (53/53 passed: 31 pre-existing lib.js tests + 22 new cli.js process tests). Both are reported here since the literal unitTestCmd was run successfully, but the scoped command is the one that actually targets this task.

Implemented case-converter/cli.js per bundle/architecture.md + bundle/requirements.json FR-1/FR-5: `-h`/`--help` before any other validation; `--text` with `--text=` form, falling back to stdin only when stdin is not a TTY (piped-but-empty stdin is valid empty input, not a missing-input error — this differs from stdin handling I observed already present in sibling utilities' cli.js, e.g. palindrome-checker/cli.js, which treats empty stdin content itself as the missing-input signal regardless of TTY-ness; I did not touch those files as they belong to other tasks, but flagging the inconsistency for the architect); `--mode` validated by lib.js's existing convert(), whose error message already lists all seven valid modes verbatim (also naturally covers the case where `--mode` is omitted entirely, since `mode === undefined` is not in MODES); `--out`/`--out=` writes the exact stdout text to the given file *in addition to* stdout, per architecture.md's explicit "stdout-plus-optional-file" contract ("вывод в stdout при этом не подавляется — --out дублирует, а не заменяет") — I noticed that word-counter/cli.js and palindrome-checker/cli.js (both already present in the working tree from other in-progress tasks) instead suppress stdout when --out is passed, which appears to contradict this documented contract; again out of scope to fix here, but worth the architect's attention since it's a cross-utility protocol inconsistency. Added `bin`/`scripts.start` to case-converter/package.json to match the per-utility package.json shape architecture.md requires (bin, start, test), which task_10 had left out since cli.js didn't exist yet. Wrote case-converter/test/cli.test.js (22 process-level tests: all 7 modes, --text/--text=, stdin fallback incl. trailing-newline stripping and empty-stdin-is-valid, --help/-h, invalid and missing --mode, --out/--out=, unwritable --out path, unicode, no-network-require static check) even though a dedicated process-test task (task_12) exists separately for this utility, since verifying my own cli.js implementation required it; task_12 can extend or reconcile with this file.
